title: Nginx
label: Nginx
desc: Serve static files and proxy HTTP traffic with a config built from server blocks and locations.

sections.title: Setup
sections.description: Install the package, test the config and reload without dropping connections.

snippets.code:
# Debian and Ubuntu ship nginx in the main repository
sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y nginx
sudo systemctl enable --now nginx

# Fedora and Arch use the same binary and unit names
sudo dnf install -y nginx
sudo pacman -S --noconfirm nginx

# Version and compile-time flags; modules are baked in, not loaded at runtime
nginx -v
nginx -V

# Test the whole config, then reload gracefully; restart only for a new binary
sudo nginx -t
sudo nginx -s reload

# Stop accepting new connections and finish the current ones
sudo nginx -s quit

sections.title: Configuration
sections.description: The main file: global settings, the events block and one http block that includes sites.

snippets.code:
# Every file the running config pulls in, in load order
sudo nginx -T | grep -E '^# configuration file'

# sites-enabled normally holds symlinks into sites-available
ls -l /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/

# Enable a site, then drop it without deleting the original
sudo ln -s /etc/nginx/sites-available/app /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/app
sudo rm /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/app

sections.title: Server Blocks
sections.description: One block per hostname: listen address, names it answers to and the default catch-all.

sections.title: Static Files
sections.description: Point root at a directory and let try_files decide between files, fallbacks and 404.

sections.title: Reverse Proxy
sections.description: Forward to an upstream app while preserving the client's host, IP and protocol.

sections.title: Headers
sections.description: Add security and CORS headers, hide upstream ones and cap request bodies.

sections.title: TLS
sections.description: Terminate HTTPS with a modern protocol set and automate renewal with certbot.

snippets.code:
# Certbot edits the server block, adds the redirect and installs the cert
sudo certbot --nginx -d example.com -d www.example.com

# Renewal runs from a systemd timer; a dry run proves it still works
sudo certbot renew --dry-run
systemctl list-timers | grep certbot

# Reload nginx after a manual renewal
sudo systemctl reload nginx

sections.title: Location Matching
sections.description: Exact, preferential prefix and regex blocks, evaluated in a fixed order.

sections.title: Rewrites
sections.description: Redirect old paths, keep slugs with captures and rewrite internally before proxying.

sections.title: Load Balancing
sections.description: Define an upstream group, pick a method and keep connections alive to the backends.

sections.title: Caching
sections.description: Cache upstream responses on disk with a key, a TTL and stale fallbacks.

snippets.code:
# How much disk the cache is using, and what is in the zone
du -sh /var/cache/nginx
sudo nginx -T | grep -A1 proxy_cache_path

# Confirm a hit on the second request
curl -sI https://example.com/api/public/status | grep -i x-cache-status

sections.title: Logs
sections.description: Shape the access log, split it per site and count what the traffic actually is.

snippets.code:
# Top ten client addresses in today's access log
sudo awk '{print $1}' /var/log/nginx/access.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -10

# Requests by status code
sudo awk '{print $9}' /var/log/nginx/access.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn

# Only errors, without blocking the terminal
sudo tail -f /var/log/nginx/error.log

# Log rotation is a logrotate hook that reopens the files
sudo logrotate -d /etc/logrotate.d/nginx

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.description: Read the config test, find the process holding a port and tell 502 from 504.

snippets.code:
# The line number in the error points at the offending file
sudo nginx -t

# Who owns the ports, and whether the config was reloaded
sudo ss -tlnp | grep -E ':80|:443'
systemctl status nginx --no-pager
sudo journalctl -u nginx -n 50 --no-pager

# Bypass DNS and the edge to test this server block directly
curl -sI --resolve example.com:443:127.0.0.1 https://example.com/

# A 413 means the body exceeded client_max_body_size
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST --data-binary @big.iso https://example.com/upload

# Too many open files shows up as "worker_connections are not enough"
ulimit -n
